detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Physics Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and aligned to AQA GCSE Physics 8463.

Thermal conduction transfers energy through a material from hotter regions to colder regions. In solids, vibrating particles transfer energy to neighbours; in metals, delocalised electrons also transfer energy rapidly, making metals good conductors.
Thermal insulators reduce the rate of energy transfer. Materials containing trapped air can be effective because air is a poor conductor when convection is prevented.

In an insulation investigation, change one factor such as insulating material or thickness, keep other variables controlled, measure temperature at regular intervals and compare the temperature decrease or cooling rate.

A valid comparison needs the same starting temperature, similar container geometry, equal volumes or masses of water, identical timing and a fair method of placing the insulation. Repeats and means improve reliability.
